thread:
Noah Patel: Need a quick decision today on model coverage for canary expansion (phase 2). We have budget for ~8 models per region without blowing the <0.5% overhead target. Let’s align on:
1) “top models” (most customer exposure)
2) “high-risk models” (likely to regress due to recent kernel/scheduler/config work)

Rina Kobayashi: I pulled last 7d request share from the prompt-set harness + usage sampling (shape-only). Top by tokens (hosted + dedicated combined):
- llama-3.1-8b-instruct
- llama-3.1-70b-instruct
- mixtral-8x7b-instruct
- qwen2.5-32b-instruct
- gemma-2-27b-it
- mistral-7b-instruct (still surprisingly high)
Embeddings are big too but diff endpoint (we can add later).

Sofia Ivanova: From scheduler side, we should include at least one “painful” large model where queueing/batching heuristics matter. llama-3.1-70b + qwen2.5-32b are good. Mixtral tends to trip weird batch composition issues too.

Hiro Tanaka: Kernel-risk list from the last two weeks:
- llama-3.1-70b: we switched default attention kernel on H100 from `fa2_sm90` to `fa3_sm90` path behind the auto-selector (see kernel tag `attn_flash_v3`). It’s faster on median but tail can be sensitive to seq-len mix.
- mixtral-8x7b: merged the grouped-gemm kernel update + new MoE routing layout. We’ve seen perf cliffs when expert parallelism meets small batches.
- gemma-2-27b: new rope scaling config + kv cache packing change (not “kernel” but touches runtime codepath).
- qwen2.5-32b: new quant profile testing (int8 weights + fp16 activations) in some pools.
If canary is meant to catch “oops the selector picked a bad kernel,” those are the ones.

Quentin Harris: For model IDs, please use canonical registry names (no alias). Proposed list (confirm):
- `llama-3.1-8b-instruct@2025-01-15`
- `llama-3.1-70b-instruct@2025-01-15`
- `mixtral-8x7b-instruct@2024-12-09`
- `qwen2.5-32b-instruct@2025-02-02`
- `gemma-2-27b-it@2025-01-20`
- `mistral-7b-instruct@2024-11-03`
We should avoid “latest” in canary config or baselines get messy.

Noah Patel: +1 on pinning versions. For “top models” I’m thinking 5-6, then 2-3 high-risk slots.
Question: do we want both 8b and 70b llama? (budget wise yes, also different shapes).

Vanessa Ortiz: Fleet note: us-east H100 pool had driver bump + minor firmware roll last week. eu-west still mixed H100/A100 for some tiers. If we want to catch infra-induced regressions, we should include at least one model that runs on both SKUs (8b + 7b). Large models are mostly H100-only.

Sofia Ivanova: Agree. Small model on A100 tends to highlight queueing-time regressions because it’s more sensitive to contention (requests complete so fast that queue dominates). For that I’d keep mistral-7b or llama-3.1-8b.

Rina Kobayashi: Synthetic prompt shapes: the current canary mix is ~70% “short” (<=512 prefill) and 30% “long” (2k-8k prefill) w/ decode up to 512 tokens. That should exercise both kernel selector and batching.
But if we add mixtral, we should ensure at least some “mid” bucket to hit expert routing patterns (I can tweak distribution but want to avoid breaking baseline comparability).

Hiro Tanaka: Please keep the distribution stable for at least a week once we expand. If we change prompt buckets same time as adding models, we’ll confuse attribution. If we need a mixtral-specific profile, do it as a separate “workload profile” flag, not a global change.

Noah Patel: That’s fair. Let’s keep global prompt distribution v0 for expansion, then add per-model profile later if needed.

Quentin Harris: One more candidate: `llama-3.1-8b-instruct` has a new “prefill fused” kernel option in one tier (not default). If canary runs across tiers, it might or might not hit it. Are we scoping canary to a single tier per region right now?

Sofia Ivanova: For MVP we said per region + one tier (hosted shared) to start, then dedicated pools later. I’d keep to that or we’ll multiply cardinality and baseline variants.

Vanessa Ortiz: +1. Also avoids accidentally fanning out to every dedicated pool.

Noah Patel: Ok. Proposed expansion set for next region rollout (top + risk):
Top exposure:
1) llama-3.1-8b-instruct
2) llama-3.1-70b-instruct
3) mixtral-8x7b-instruct
4) qwen2.5-32b-instruct
5) gemma-2-27b-it
6) mistral-7b-instruct
High-risk (if we have 2 extra slots):
7) llama-3.1-70b-instruct (already in) so maybe not separate
7) (alt) `llama-3.1-70b-instruct` but force long-context profile? (not now)
7) `deepseek-r1-distill-llama-8b`? (newly onboarded) — not sure usage yet
8) `llama-3.1-8b-instruct` on A100? (but tier restriction)

Need better “high-risk but not already top” candidates.

Hiro Tanaka: High-risk but not top: anything that just got a kernel change. Right now the kernel changes mostly hit the top list already.
If you want distinct: pick one of the “recently onboarded” models where the selector coverage is thin. Example: `qwen2.5-72b-instruct` (we only have partial benchmarking) or `yi-34b-chat` (older but weird).
But I’d rather spend slots on models with customer impact.

Rina Kobayashi: Usage for qwen2.5-72b is low-ish but growing. It also pushes long-context usage more.
If we add it, we should ensure canary includes at least some >4k prompts (already does 30% long).

Sofia Ivanova: Another “high-risk” dimension is recent scheduler tweaks. The last patch to continuous batching had a change to “max prefill tokens per batch” default. That affects *everything*, but the impact shows up more on large models + long prompts. So llama-70b + qwen-32b + (optional) qwen-72b is the triad.

Noah Patel: Sounds like: keep top 6 list, add qwen2.5-72b as “risk/long context” slot. That gets us to 7.
We have room for 1 more.

Vanessa Ortiz: For infra sensitivity, add something that runs on A100 in eu-west (since that’s where the mixed pool is). But if we keep one tier, we might still be H100-only depending on routing.
Could we add `llama-3.1-8b-instruct` but pin the canary target hardware via config in eu-west? (only if the config supports SKU targeting).

Noah Patel: We do have per-region hardware SKU config in the canary (from the recent config PR) but we’ve been avoiding multi-SKU in same region. Maybe we do: eu-west runs canary on A100 for 8b/7b model only; everything else stays H100.
This is exactly the kind of thing that caused baseline drift earlier though :/.

Hiro Tanaka: If you do that, make it explicit in the baseline key: model+version+sku. Don’t let it silently mix. Otherwise we’ll be back in alert storm land.

Quentin Harris: +1. Also please don’t call it “A100” in labels; use canonical SKU string (e.g., `nvidia-a100-80gb` vs `nvidia-h100-sxm`). We already have the mapping in registry.

Sofia Ivanova: Candidate for the 8th slot: `llama-3.1-8b-instruct` but *only* in eu-west A100, because that’s where we’ve seen the scheduler queue metric look odd. That gives us a signal on “infra + scheduler” without adding a whole new model.

Noah Patel: Ok, decision:
Core list (all regions, H100 where applicable):
- llama-3.1-8b-instruct
- llama-3.1-70b-instruct
- mixtral-8x7b-instruct
- qwen2.5-32b-instruct
- gemma-2-27b-it
- mistral-7b-instruct
Risk add:
- qwen2.5-72b-instruct (long-context + partial kernel coverage)
Infra/scheduler validation:
- llama-3.1-8b-instruct on eu-west `nvidia-a100-80gb` (explicit sku key)

Rina: can you confirm prompt distribution v0 is still representative for 72b? If not we’ll accept it for now.
Hiro: anything else that’s “kernel changed yesterday” we’re missing?

Rina Kobayashi: Works. v0 should hit enough long prompts to exercise 72b. I’ll add a note in the config doc that 72b baselines will have higher variance and we might need larger min sample.

Hiro Tanaka: No other kernel bombshells. Only ask: make sure canary emits the kernel tag + runtime build id. For llama-70b we need to see `attn_flash_v3` vs `attn_flash_v2` split in the dashboard or it’s not actionable.

Noah Patel: Yep, kernel tag is already in telemetry for canary runs. I’ll double-check the dashboard has a filter and that alerts include it in the payload.

Mateo Alvarez: :thumbsup: This list looks right. Prioritize customer impact. If we catch one real regression in the next rollout wave, this will have paid for itself.
One request: in the rollout checklist, explicitly call out “new kernel selector changes” as a reason to add a model to high-risk list.

Noah Patel: Will do. I’ll post the final list in the rollout ticket + ask Nadia/Logan to sanity check baseline storage keys for the eu-west A100 split.

Vanessa Ortiz: I’ll sync with fleet on eu-west A100 stability window so we don’t baseline during a churny day.

Quentin Harris: I’ll make sure the registry version pins are correct + no aliases. Please paste the final canonical strings when you update config.

Noah Patel: Closing the loop here once config is merged. Thanks all.
